caption: FM modulation index at depth. Top panel: the carrier and each sideband pair trade power as the index grows - their amplitudes are the Bessel functions Jn(index), so the carrier shrinks (and even phase-reverses) while more sideband pairs become significant. The pool's numbers are dashed: deviation ratios 1.67 (5 kHz / 3 kHz, E8B05) and 2.14 (7.5 kHz / 3.5 kHz, E8B06), and index 3. Bottom panel: the line spectrum at index 3 - both pool index calculations land here (3000/1000 = 3, E8B03; 6000/2000 = 3, E8B04). The carrier drops to 0.26 of its unmodulated strength, sideband pairs sit at fc plus-or-minus n times the modulating frequency, and the significant sidebands reach about plus-or-minus (index + 1) times f_mod. Index = deviation / modulating frequency; deviation ratio is the same shape built from the MAXIMUM deviation and HIGHEST modulating frequency - and every calculation question offers the inverted ratio as the distractor.
spoken: The top panel plots five curves against modulation index: the carrier's amplitude and the first four sideband pairs, each a Bessel function of the index. The carrier starts at full strength and falls, crossing through zero into a phase-reversed lobe, while the sideband pairs rise one after another - power is leaving the carrier for the sidebands. Three dashed vertical lines mark the pool's own numbers: deviation ratio 1.67, deviation ratio 2.14, and index 3. The bottom panel draws the actual spectrum at index 3, the value both pool index calculations key to: eleven lines spaced by the modulating frequency around the carrier. The center line, the carrier, is down to 0.26 of its unmodulated strength; the second sideband pair is the tallest at 0.49; and the significant lines reach out to about plus-or-minus four times the modulating frequency - index plus one. The exam arithmetic sits underneath: index equals deviation divided by modulating frequency, deviation ratio equals maximum deviation divided by highest modulating frequency, and the inverted ratio is always a distractor - divide deviation by the modulating frequency, never the reverse.
